query:
The group at some point treated it as a shared street understanding that short-term Airbnb-style rentals are not done on Maple Street. Does this view actually apply to everyone? If not, which group member expressed a different position and what specifically did they say?

Options:
A. Sandra
B. Dev
C. Yuki
D. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Sandra, episodic, t6 @2025-11-02T12:43:00) I did see it. I assumed they were just letting friends stay. We did agree as a street that we would not do short-term rentals commercially -- that was discussed at the association meeting two years ago. -- Sandra
[2] (about=Dev, episodic, t6 @2025-11-02T12:47:00) i mean it's their house. not really our call
[3] (about=Yuki, episodic, t6 @2025-11-02T12:54:00) Honestly this is genuinely interesting to me from a research angle. Like the fact that there's a norm that not everyone agreed to but gets enforced as a collective agreement.
[4] (about=Claire, episodic, t6 @2025-11-02T12:45:00) Exactly. I've raised this twice and been told it's a personal choice but it genuinely changes things. You get strangers with rolling suitcases at 11pm and then the whole atmosphere is different.
[5] (about=Claire, episodic, t6 @2025-11-02T12:40:00) Different topic -- I saw a sign outside number 6 saying 'available on Airbnb' with a QR code. Did anyone else see that?
[6] (about=Sandra, episodic, t8 @2025-11-16T11:12:00) Just a quick note to say that we are all very sorry to hear this, though of course we wish you every happiness with the new role. Maple Street will not be the same without you. When my husband was alive he always said you could tell the quality of a street by how much it missed the people who left. -- Sandra
[7] (about=Sandra, episodic, t6 @2025-11-02T13:00:00) I think it matters that we agree on what kind of street we want to be. That is not enforcement, that is community. But I also think yesterday showed that when we just get together and enjoy each other's company we are a good group. Let us not get too tangled up in the rules. -- Sandra
[8] (about=Sandra, episodic, t1 @2025-10-19T11:02:00) Just a quick note: I heard back from the residents' association about the parking changes. Apparently the council is proposing to remove two spaces outside numbers 8 and 10 to widen the pavement. Consultation closes Friday. I will be responding on behalf of the street but I think we should discuss it first rather than just me speaking for everyone. -- Sandra
[9] (about=Sandra, episodic, t12 @2025-11-30T12:04:00) They should have sent it to all residents, not just owners. I'll mention it at the next meeting. In the meantime I'll put your vote down alongside mine if you tell me your preference. -- Sandra
[10] (about=Marcus, episodic, t4 @2025-10-26T11:33:00) probably move. rent here's getting stupid
[11] (about=Claire, core, t6 @2025-11-02T12:17:00) Claire opposes the Airbnb rental, having raised it twice and been told it's a personal choice, but feels it changes the street's atmosphere.
[12] (about=Claire, core, t6 @2025-11-02T12:17:00) Claire saw a sign outside number 6 saying 'available on Airbnb' with a QR code.
[13] (about=Dev, core, t6 @2025-11-02T12:17:00) Dev thinks the Airbnb is their house and not really the group's call.
[14] (about=Marcus, core, t4 @2025-10-26T10:48:00) Said rent in his current area is getting stupid, which is a reason he'd consider moving.
[15] (about=Marcus, core, t6 @2025-11-02T12:17:00) Marcus doesn't see a problem with the Airbnb if they're quiet about it.
[16] (about=Sandra, core, t6 @2025-11-02T12:17:00) Sandra saw the Airbnb sign and assumed they were letting friends stay, recalling the street agreed not to do short-term rentals commercially at the association meeting two years ago.
[17] (about=GROUP, said_by=Sandra, group-interaction, t6 @2025-11-02T12:17:00) Group discussed the Airbnb at number 6, with Claire and Sandra opposing it, Dev and Marcus not seeing a problem, and Yuki noting the norm enforcement.
[18] (about=Yuki, core, t6 @2025-11-02T12:17:00) Yuki finds the Airbnb situation interesting from a research angle, noting a norm not everyone agreed to but enforced as collective agreement.
